SMTO-GIT-0001 — SMTO couldn't find a Git project in that folder

GUID: 359aea4d-8513-4806-8735-97c7a6574144
Slug: git-repository-absent
Domain: GIT · Subsystem: git

What happened

  • SMTO looked for a Git project (a folder whose history is tracked with Git) in the folder it was using, and didn't find one. Nothing in that folder was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check that the folder you gave SMTO is the project folder or a folder inside it; the project folder contains a hidden .git folder or file. SMTO recognizes a Git project by that hidden .git entry.
  2. If the project was moved, renamed or deleted on that Gateway computer, give SMTO its new location. SMTO only checks the location it was told about, so an old location no longer matches.
  3. Only if you really want a new Git project there, ask SMTO to create one with git init in that folder. Creating a project in the wrong folder would start tracking files you didn't mean to.

What success looks like

  • SMTO shows the project's details, such as its main folder, without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway computer. If this is part of a saved Run, change its folder yourself; don't let it be switched to a different project without checking.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gateway Git discovery checked the selected directory and up to 64 parent levels (or only that directory, for an exact or previously known root) without finding a .git directory, a gitdir file or a bare repository (HEAD plus objects/).

What this means

  • Repository discovery reaches the exact-directory boundary or filesystem root without finding a .git marker or supported bare-repository structure. These checks validate repository identity/observation. Failure of an optional observation does not establish failure or rollback of the Git command whose receipt carries it; no diagnostic rewrites Git metadata.

Why this can happen

  • Repository discovery reaches the exact-directory boundary or filesystem root without finding a .git marker or supported bare-repository structure.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the selected Gateway-native directory and whether exact lookup or parent search was requested.

How to fix it

  • On the Gateway host, run git rev-parse --show-toplevel in the selected directory, and check whether a previously known root was moved or deleted (it is reported as a stale root). Point the command or saved run at the intended existing repository; run git init only if creating a repository is part of the requested work.
  • Choose the intended repository directory. Initialize a repository only if creating one is part of the requested work.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Discovery locates the intended existing repository and reports its native root.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • These checks validate repository identity/observation. Failure of an optional observation does not establish failure or rollback of the Git command whose receipt carries it; no diagnostic rewrites Git metadata.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
